tweets.text: It amazes me how many managers operate under the "push people/teams until they crack and then back off a tad" philosophy.

I discovered yesterday that you can collect ideas in a document. You don't need to put them in Jira?!?!?!

It is wild. You write them....but w/o a ticket number assigned.

No Project GODOT-18. No status "waiting". No "watchers". No status.

You write it. Just write it.
OH: “strategy is sitting around in an offsite until we give up and agree with each other”
Two level, hybrid boards are incredibly effective …. Yet a huge PIA to do in most tools.

my god ... some orgs/teams are starting annual planning

sending strength.
Your company is optimized to avoid the hardest conversations it needs to have

The shift from “how can we get the most out of IT at the lowest cost” to “‘how we use design, technology, and data as a competitive advantage” is a big one.

you can swap words … “project” with “product”, but the former mindset is deeply entrenched.

product management:

get specific
"need big picture"

big picture
"too vague"

hands on
"hands off"

hands off
"hands on"

more context
"less meeting time"

less meeting time
"more context"

small efforts
"less optimizing"

big missions
"more small stuff"

(repeat)
The big warning a give during my north star framework workshops...

LinkedIn

“If we usability test it and need to make changes does that count as two stories or one? Wouldn’t the team be getting credit twice?”

There not a great way to say this but

…. IT DOES NOT MATTER STORY POINTS ARE NOT REAL

How does an organization "forget"?

One way ... there's a push for operational efficiency in the midst of increasing complexity.

The organizations loses people with institutional knowledge, and starts mischaracterizing the challenge as one of operational efficiency.
